# Geographical Potential

## Row {height="auto"}

### Column {width="65%"}

<span style="font-size: 2rem;font-weight: bold">Analysis Overview</span>

As electricity demand grows across British Columbia, more renewable energy installations need to be developed to support a resilient, diversified, low-carbon future. In light of this challenge, a site suitability analysis was undergone to create a province-wide screening tool that determines the most optimal locations for solar PV development.

The [Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0270025587904738) was used to combine heterogeneous input criteria into a single, comprehensive suitability model. Through expert consultation with professionals across academia, policy, and industry, weights were assigned to each criteria representing their relative importance in the siting process. The following table outlines the criteria, definitions, and weights used to rank the province's landscape, providing a rigorous, data-driven foundation for our site selection analysis.

Prior to criteria weighting, a land constraint layer was applied to exclude restricted areas from the analysis, including:

* Protected and Conserved Areas: Provincial/federal parks, ecological reserves, and protected watersheds.
* Unsuitable Land Covers: Water bodies, wetlands, permanent snow and ice, and artificial/built environments 
* Dense Forests: stands with a canopy cover greater than 40% 
* Agricultural Land Reserve: Filtered to Soil Capability Classes 1-3
* Linear Infrastructure: All roads and railways

Explore the map below to see how the distribition of land constraints and suitability classes across the province, along side the locations of BC's 12 existing solar installations.

#| echo: false

import pandas as pd
from great_tables import GT
from great_tables import style
from great_tables import loc

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Criteria": [
        "Proximity to the Grid",
        "Global Tilted Irradiance",
        "Proximity to Demand Centers",
        "Proximity to Major Roads",
        "Ground Aspect",
        "Ground Slope",
    ],
    "Impact/Definition": [
        "High-voltage transmission infrastructure is expensive to construct. Proximity to existing substations minimizes interconnection costs and improves project economics",
        "The total solar radiation received by a panel tilted toward the sun, accounting for direct, diffuse, and ground-reflected light",
        "Siting generation near major load centers minimizes transmission line losses and reduces grid congestion",
        "Proximity to transportation networks lowers site construction costs, simplifies heavy equipment haulage, and ensures long-term operational access",
        "Topographic orientation relative to the sun. In the Northern Hemisphere, south-facing slopes maximize annual solar energy yield",
        "Terrain steepness. Gentle or flat terrain minimizes civil grading costs, simplifies tracker/mounting installation, and prevents inter-row panel shading",
    ],
    "Weight": ["30.2%", "26.3%", "14.4%", "11.2%", "9.3%", "8.5%"],
})

table = (
    GT(df)
    # Bold column headers
    .tab_style( 
        style=style.text(weight="bold"),
        locations=loc.column_labels()
    )
    # Center column headers 
    .tab_style(
        style=style.text(align="center"),
        locations=loc.column_labels()
    )
    # Fill column headers with a light blue color
    .tab_style(
        style=style.fill(color="#5b89aad2"),
        locations=loc.column_labels()
    )
)

table
```

import folium
import leafmap.foliumap as leafmap

import json

    1: [255, 255, 178, 255],  # #FFFFB2
    2: [254, 204, 92, 255],   # #FECC5C
    3: [253, 141, 60, 255],   # #FD8D3C
    4: [240, 59, 32, 255],    # #F03B20
    5: [189, 0, 38, 255]      # #BD0026
}

# Ask TiTiler to build the tile URL template using your exact color palette
r = requests.get(
    f"{titiler_endpoint}/cog/WebMercatorQuad/tilejson.json",
    params={
        "url": cog_url,
        "colormap": json.dumps(custom_colormap),
        "nodata": "nan",
    },
).json()

tile_url = r["tiles"][0]

m = leafmap.Map(center=[54.000, -128.000], zoom=5)

# Add Regional Districts from GitHub

    "Class 4",
    "Class 5",
]

    "District:",
    "Class 1 Area (km²):",
    "Class 2 Area (km²):",
    "Class 3 Area (km²):",

]

district_tooltip = folium.GeoJsonTooltip(

)

        "fillColor": "grey",

import pandas as pd

    "0": "0 - Restricted", "1": "1 - Least Suitable", "2": "2 - Less Suitable",
    "3": "3 - Moderately Suitable", "4": "4 - Suitable", "5": "5 - Very Suitable"

    "0": "#696969", "1": "#FFFFB2", "2": "#FECC5C",

# Create and configure the bar chart
fig = (px.bar(
    suit_df,
    x="Suitability Class",

    hover_data=['percent_of_total']
)
.update_traces(
    hovertemplate="<b>%{x}</b><br>Area: %{y:,.0f} km²<br>Percent of BC: %{customdata[0]:.2f}%<extra></extra>"

    hovermode='x unified'
)

.update_xaxes(

))

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import display

# Read the regional district CSV
rd_df = pd.read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenzthom/SolarModel_Dash/main/data/suitability_regDis.csv')

# Filter to only Class 4 and 5
df_high = rd_df[rd_df['class'].isin(['Class 4', 'Class 5'])].copy()

# Group by district and sum area
df_grouped = df_high.groupby('district_name')['Area_km2'].sum().reset_index()
df_grouped = df_grouped.sort_values('Area_km2')

# Create label alias so regional district is not repeated in every label 
df_grouped["alias"] = (df_grouped["district_name"]
    .str.replace('Regional District of', '')
    .str.replace('Regional District', ''))

# Create bar chart
fig = (px.bar(
    df_grouped,
    y="alias",
    x="Area_km2",
    orientation='h',
    labels={"alias": "Regional District", "Area_km2": "Area (km²)"},
    color_discrete_sequence=['#e54608']
)

.update_traces(
    hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>Area: %{x:,.0f} km²<extra></extra>"
)

.update_layout(
    yaxis_title="Regional District",
    xaxis_title="Area Class 4 & 5 (km²)",
    showlegend=False,
    hovermode='y unified'
))

fig
```

# Technical Potential

## Row

### Column {width ="75%"}

<span style="font-size: 2rem;font-weight: bold">Solar Resource Potential</span>

Technical potential translates suitable land area into electricity generation capabilities. We calculated installable capacity (GW) for each viable site using the parcel's area, a 23% panel efficiency, latitude-dependent Ground Cover Ratios, and a Packing Density Ratio. Annual energy yield draws from PVout (potential photovoltaic output) values for each site. Yield estimates are based on a 1 MW minimum production threshold, providing a realistic assessment of the province's solar energy potential ceiling.

To illustrate the spectrum of development opportunities, the map distinguishes between two development pathways: +2 MW sites within municipal boundaries (community-scale installations) and +100 MW sites outside municipal boundaries (utility-scale installations). These dual pathways reflect BC's capacity to meet renewable energy targets through both distributed and centralized generation.

Explore the map below to see the raw photovoltaic resource distribution across the province, viable site locations at different scales, and total capacity and annual energy yield across BC's regional districts.

# Case Study: Thompson-Nicola Regional District

## Row {height="auto"}

<span style="font-size: 2rem;font-weight: bold">From Screening to Site Selection</span>

TOPSIS – Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution – is a methodological extension of AHP used to rank alternatives based on their geometric distance from ideal and non-ideal solutions. This approach identifies sites that simultaneously maximize desirable criteria (e.g., high irradiance, proximity to substations) while minimizing undesirable ones (e.g., steep terrain, north facing aspects).

We applied TOPSIS to the Thompson-Nicola Regional District (TNRD) as a detailed case study, ranking all eligible sites within the region to identify priority development locations. Notably, the top-ranked site aligns with the location of the proposed Nicola Lake Solar Farm, validating the methodology's capacity to identify viable development opportunities. This analysis demonstrates how the suitability framework translates into actionable site-level investment decisions at the regional scale. 

Explore the map and table below to see the ranked sites across the Thompson-Nicola Regional District, with top-ranked sites indicating the strongest candidates for development.

## Row

### Column {width=30%}

```{python}
import geopandas as gpd

tn_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenzthom/SolarModel_Dash/main/data/tn_topsis.geojson" 
munis_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenzthom/SolarModel_Dash/main/data/municipalities.geojson"

sites = gpd.read_file(tn_url)
munis = gpd.read_file(munis_url) 

# Filter top 10 sites
sites = sites.sort_values(by='rank', ascending=True).head(10).copy() 

# Reproject to epsg=3005 for distance calc
sites_proj = sites.to_crs(epsg=3005)
munis_proj = munis.to_crs(epsg=3005)

# Use spatial join to find muni closest to each top 10 site
joined = gpd.sjoin_nearest(
    sites_proj,
    munis_proj[['AA_NAME', 'geometry']],
    how='left'
)

# Make clean summary 
sites_summary = (
    joined[['rank', 'cpct_MW', 'enrg_TW', 'AA_NAME_right']]
    .round(1)
    .rename(columns={
        "rank": "Site Rank",
        "cpct_MW": "Capacity (MW)",
        "enrg_TW": "Annual Energy (TWh)",
        "AA_NAME_right": "Nearest Municipality"
    })
)

# Make appearence match first page table
table = (
    GT(sites_summary)
    # Bold column headers
    .tab_style( 
        style=style.text(weight="bold"),
        locations=loc.column_labels()
    )
    # Fill column headers with a light blue color
    .tab_style(
        style=style.fill(color="#5b89aad2"),
        locations=loc.column_labels()
    )
)

table
```

#| title: "TNRD PV Site Ranking Map"

import folium
import leafmap.foliumap as leafmap
import requests
import json
import geopandas as gpd

# Define a rule-based color function
def get_color(feature):
    rank = feature['properties'].get('rank')
    if rank <= 10:
        return '#cb0909'  
    elif rank > 10 and rank <= 100:
        return '#ea5312'  
    elif rank > 100 and rank <= 1000:
        return '#fe9423'
    else:
        return '#FECC5C'  


m = leafmap.Map(center=[51.000, -121.000], zoom=7)
m.add_basemap("HYBRID")

# Add thompson nicola boundary from GitHub
bound_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenzthom/SolarModel_Dash/main/data/thompson_nicola.geojson"

_ = folium.GeoJson(
    bound_url,
    embed=False,
    name="Thompson-Nicola Boundary",
    style_function=lambda x: {
        "fillColor": "grey",
        "fillOpacity": 0.0, 
        "color": "#FCE32A",
        "weight": 1.5,
    },
    control=True,
).add_to(m)

tn_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kenzthom/SolarModel_Dash/main/data/tn_topsis.geojson" 

# Define tooltip columns (District Name + your 5 suitability classes)
rank_cols = ["rank",
            "Are_km2",
            "cpct_MW",
            "enrg_TW"]

tooltip_aliases = ["Rank:",
                   "Area (km²):",
                   "Capacity (MW):",
                   "Annual Energy (TWh):"]

tn_tooltip = folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
    fields=rank_cols,
    aliases=tooltip_aliases,
    localize=True,
    labels=True,
    sticky=False,  
)

_ = folium.GeoJson(
    tn_url,
    embed=False, 
    name="Thompson-Nicola Regional District TOPSIS Ranking",
    tooltip=tn_tooltip,  
    control=True,
    style_function=lambda feature: {
        'fillColor': get_color(feature),
        'color': 'black',       
        'weight': 0.5,           
        'fillOpacity': 0.9
}

).add_to(m)

# Layer control
_ = folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)

# Add custom legend using html
legend_html = '''

     background-color: white; border:2px solid grey; z-index:9999;
